Non-contrast/contrast-enhanced CT abdomen/pelvis — though negative for mass, calculi, lymphadenopathy, or retroperitoneal abnormality — has well-documented limitations for detecting flat or small urothelial tumors, particularly in the renal pelvis or ureter, especially without dedicated excretory-phase imaging (i.e., CT urography). The lack of renal ultrasound, serum creatinine, eGFR, BP, or smoking history leaves key risk stratification incomplete — but the clinical constellation remains highly suspicious for UTUC. While other entities (e.g., renal arteriovenous malformation, IgA nephropathy, thin basement membrane disease) can cause isolated hematuria, they rarely present with *flank discomfort* and are typically associated with microscopic (not gross) hematuria, often with normal imaging — and none explain the combination of painless gross hematuria + flank discomfort + negative cystoscopy + negative non-urographic CT.

[EVIDENCE]  
- Painless gross hematuria (classic presentation of urothelial carcinoma)  
- Right flank discomfort (suggestive of upper tract involvement, e.g., pelvic/ureteral tumor causing irritation or partial obstruction)  
- Absence of lower urinary tract symptoms (reduces likelihood of benign prostatic disease or cystitis)  
- No pyuria, bacteriuria, or RBC casts on urinalysis (argues against infection, glomerulonephritis, or vasculitis)  
- Unremarkable cystoscopy (rules out bladder cancer as source)  
- CT abdomen/pelvis shows no renal/ureteral calculi, no mass, no lymphadenopathy, no retroperitoneal abnormality — but was not specified as CT urography (i.e., lacks excretory phase), limiting sensitivity for urothelial tumors  

[GAPS]  
- CT urography (excretory-phase imaging) not performed or reported  
- Renal ultrasound results not documented  
- Serum creatinine and eGFR unavailable (limits assessment of renal function and chronicity)  
- Blood pressure measurement not reported (hypertension may suggest underlying renal parenchymal disease)  
- Smoking history, occupational exposures (e.g., aromatic amines), prior cyclophosphamide or analgesic use not documented

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Upper tract urothelial carcinoma
